text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to $150.80, capping a 12.45% surge over two weeks. The timing aligns directly with escalating Middle East tensions: Saudi Arabia intercepted Iranian-backed Houthi missiles and drones on October 25th, Brent crude topped $116 a barrel (a six-month high) on October 23rd, and oil prices have remained elevated above $107 per barrel for U.S. crude. As a major oil producer, the company benefits when geopolitical risk pushes energy prices higher.

The broader pattern here is that U.S. energy companies are gaining as the Iran-related conflict reshapes global markets — a trend that extends beyond just crude producers to liquefied natural gas exporters and refiners with exposure to higher feedstock values. Today's move appears to be a continuation of that momentum rather than a single-day catalyst.
